assets.title: Containing a routine voice call without an agent
assets.summary: A customer calls to reschedule a delivery. The AI agent understands the request in natural language, checks the order, offers new slots, and confirms, with no human involved and no menu tree.

chapters.label: The call arrives
chapters.talkTrack: Watch what does not happen here. No menu, no press one for deliveries. The caller just says what they want.

chapters.label: Understanding intent
chapters.talkTrack: The agent has resolved two things at once: the intent, and the specific order. That order lookup is a tool call into the backend, not scripted.

chapters.label: Offering options
chapters.talkTrack: Slot availability is live. This is the part that usually forces a transfer to a human, and it is the part that most determines whether containment holds.

chapters.label: Confirmation
chapters.talkTrack: Confirmed and logged. If any step had failed, the escalation path would have carried the full context to a human rather than starting over.

talkingPoints: Natural language, no menu navigation required
Live backend lookup via tool calls rather than scripted responses
Failure path preserves context for the human agent

assets.title: AI to human escalation without losing context
assets.summary: When the AI agent cannot complete a request, the conversation moves to a human agent who arrives with the full transcript, the resolved customer record, and a summary of what was already tried.

chapters.label: Recognising the limit
chapters.talkTrack: The agent does not loop or apologise repeatedly. It recognises it is out of scope and escalates, which is a design choice you control.

chapters.label: Routing to the right skill
chapters.talkTrack: Routing uses the intent that was already established, so the customer does not repeat themselves to a human.

chapters.label: What the human sees
chapters.talkTrack: This is the screen that matters. Transcript, customer record, and a generated summary. Handle time savings live here.

talkingPoints: Escalation criteria are configurable, not model-dependent
Human agent receives a generated summary

assets.title: Building the AI agent, step by step
assets.summary: A clickable walkthrough of how the AI agent above was actually configured: the agent definition, its tools, the knowledge source, and the escalation rule.

steps.caption: The agent definition. Persona and rails, no dialogue tree.
The tools available to the agent. The model chooses which to call.
The escalation rule. Deterministic, not left to the model.

talkingPoints: Agentic design replaces large dialogue trees
Tool definitions are the main build artefact

assets.title: How the pieces fit together
assets.summary: An architecture view of the platform layer: channels, the AI agent, knowledge, routing, and the analytics loop that feeds improvements back in.
talkingPoints: Analytics feeds agent improvement rather than sitting in a separate report

tours.title: Automate more without frustrating customers
tours.goal: The visitor understands that containment and customer experience are not in tension, because the escalation path is designed rather than accidental.

steps.narration: Let me start with the case everyone worries about: a routine call that a bot would normally mangle.
steps.checkIn: Is that closer to your current self-service experience, or quite far from it?

steps.narration: Now the more important half. Containment only works if the failure path is good, so here is what happens when the AI agent hits its limit.
steps.checkIn: How much of your handle time today goes on customers repeating themselves?

steps.narration: Last one, and this is for whoever on your side will ask how it actually plugs in.
steps.checkIn: Would it help to go deeper on the integration side with one of our architects?
